articles.title: ‘Maybe I’m just getting older’: Naomi Osaka’s surprising reaction after US Open exit
articles.summary: Tennis News: Naomi Osaka's US Open campaign came to an end in the fourth round, but the former world No. 1 walked away from Flushing Meadows with a sense of perspe.
articles.body: Naomi Osaka's US Open campaign came to an end in the fourth round, but the former world No. 1 walked away from Flushing Meadows with a sense of perspective rather than disappointment.The two-time US Open champion was beaten by Elena Rybakina in a one-sided contest on Monday, ending a run that had also seen Osaka once again capture attention away from the court with a series of eye-catching fashion statements.Yet when she addressed the media after the defeat, Osaka's focus was less on the loss and more on the bigger picture.Asked whether she was disappointed that her exit meant fans would not get to see some of the other fashion looks she may have planned for later rounds, Osaka admitted there was always something in the works."I think there's always something [laughs]. That's a way that I can have fun and sort of just excite myself also. But I'm honestly not disappointed now. It's a very strange feeling. And last year I wasn't that disappointed either. Amanda just played really insane. Maybe I'm just getting older, but I don't feel sad."‘I'm happy I'm taking losses differently’The four-time Grand Slam champion was then asked whether she was surprised by her reaction to the defeat, given that losses had often affected her more deeply earlier in her career.Osaka said she has learned to process setbacks differently and now looks for lessons rather than dwelling on disappointment."I think I'm happy I'm taking losses differently. I'm trying to learn from them a lot more. Today if I was to say I'm sad, I was sad that I couldn't push off on my foot. I'm sad I couldn't do what I set out to do."The 28-year-old revealed she had been troubled by pain in her leg during the match against Rybakina, which affected her movement on court.Still, she stressed that tennis results no longer define her outlook on life."But for me if I think about my life, my daughter is healthy. Everyone in my family is great. I had an opportunity to play this Slam. I got as far as I could. It's only up from here I guess."Osaka's fashion showcase lights up New YorkAlthough her tournament ended in the fourth round, Osaka remained one of the standout personalities of the event thanks to a string of fashion-forward appearances inspired by basketball culture.With sponsor Nike celebrating the New York Knicks' championship triumph, Osaka unveiled a different look throughout the tournament, working alongside celebrity stylist Law Roach.For her final appearance, she arrived on court wearing a fur-trimmed multicoloured cloak designed by Brooklyn-based label KidSuper."I felt really swaggy when I put it on," Osaka said after the match. "I feel feel like it embodied New York a lot."The outfit also featured a headband inspired by the NBA logo, replacing the traditional basketball player silhouette with a tennis player holding a racket.Earlier in the tournament, Osaka paid tribute to NBA legend Allen Iverson with a dramatic first-round ensemble designed by Who Decides War, featuring a long white tulle skirt, a hooded robe and cornrows beneath a headband reminiscent of Iverson's iconic style.Her second-round look came from Thom Browne and included a flowing white jacket embroidered with crossed tennis rackets, while the mesh fabric of her skirt was designed to resemble a basketball net.For the third round, she wore an oversized Monse outfit that blended a suit jacket and hoodie with flowing fleece trousers, combining businesswear and sportswear aesthetics.‘If I win another Grand Slam, it's not going to change my life’Osaka's comments after the loss reflected a broader shift in how she now views her career and achievements.While still motivated to compete at the highest level, the former world No. 1 suggested that winning another major title would not fundamentally alter her life or sense of fulfilment.Reflecting on everything she has already achieved in the sport, Osaka indicated she no longer measures happiness solely through victories and trophies."Maybe I'm just getting older, but I don't feel sad," Osaka said. "I think, also, if I reflect on my career and the things that I've been able to do, there's nothing that I regret or there's nothing that I'm sad about ... If I win another Grand Slam, it's not going to change my life."For Osaka, the US Open may have ended earlier than she hoped, but her reaction to defeat suggested a player increasingly at peace with both her career and her life beyond tennis.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: El Zverev de siempre ya está en cuartos de final
articles.standfirst: El alemán vuelve a convencer ante Darderi y es el primero en llegar a las 50 victorias esta temporada
articles.summary: El alemán vuelve a convencer ante Darderi y es el primero en llegar a las 50 victorias esta temporada
articles.body: Alexander Zverev continúa con su temporada estelar en los Grand Slam. Por cuarta vez este año, ha certificado su pase a los cuartos de final de un grande, el único jugador en hacerlo. En esta ocasión, ha derrotado al italiano Luciano Darderi por 6-2, 6-2 y 7-6 (3) en otro gran desempeño. Sascha, que en sus dos primeros partidos en Flushing Meadows llegó a sumar 10 horas en pista, ha cambiado el guion de su torneo. En el duelo de tercera ronda con Tabilo, y hoy ante Darderi, ha conseguido dos valiosas victorias en tres mangas. Cabe recordar que los cuatro partidos diputados hasta el momento del alemán, han sido en el segundo turno nocturno de la Arthur Ashe. Condiciones que parecen sentarle bien al tenista de Hamburgo. Zverev tenía muy claro como salir hoy. Agresivo y enchufado desde el primer punto, más si cabe sabiendo de la pegada que tiene el italiano. Todo estuvo marcado por el servicio del alemán, que elevó su porcentaje de primeros hasta un 72%, adjudicándose 51 de 59 (86%) puntos con una de sus mayores armas. Sascha empezó marcando su terreno rompiendo el saque de su rival en el juego inicial del partido. Las dos primeras mangas siguieron la misma tónica, el alemán, incontestable tanto al servicio como al resto, y Darderi sin saber por donde tirar. Hasta 17 bolas de 'break' llegó a fabricarse el primer cabeza de serie del torneo. El tercer set necesitó del tie-break para decidir el último cuartofinalista del cuadro masculino. El italiano había subido de gran manera en el encuentro de la mano de su mejora al primer servicio. Pero la regularidad del alemán tuvo premio (su récord en tie-breaks en 2026 es de 28-13) y lo cerró por 7-3. Zverev, ya con un nivel más parecido al que le hizo campeón en la tierra de París y finalista en Wimbledon, está entre los ocho mejores del US Open. Con sus 19 cuartos de final, Sascha es el segundo tenista en activo que más veces ha pisado esta ronda. Ya ha superado a Stan Wawrinka (18), y solo tiene por encima a Novak Djokovic (66). Su próximo objetivo será el holandés Botic Van de Zandschulp, que viene de derrotar al lucky-loser Arthur Gea en 5:13 h de partido, el cuarto más largo en la historia del torneo.

articles.title: US Open 2026: Home favourite Coco Gauff wins all-American showdown with Iva Jovic to reach quarter-finals
articles.summary: An impressive victory for Coco Gauff sets up a last-eight meeting with French Open champion Mirra Andreeva; Gauff is aiming to win the US Open for a second time in her career; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis
articles.body:
The 22-year-old, who is bidding for a second Flushing Meadows title, overpowered Jovic 6-1, 6-4 on a balmy Labour Day bank holiday night in New York.

A jittery start from the 2023 winner gifted 18-year-old Jovic a break in the first game with a double fault.

But Jovic's nerves were also on show as Gauff raced away with the next six games to take the first set.

Jovic finally held serve at the start of the second but three spectacular Gauff hustles, turning desperate defence into all-out attack, secured a break for 3-2.

The youngster managed to hit straight back, but was then broken to love as Gauff took control before serving out to win in an hour and 33 minutes.

Gauff, who is yet to drop a set so far, made sure to reassure Jovic that her time will come: "Iva's an incredible player, an incredible talent, she plays beyond her years. I'm used to being the younger American!

"I thought today was a good match for me. The first set was really high-level and she raised her level in the second.

"I had some opportunities to maybe get up some early breaks. We're all just happy with how I was able to close the last game out.

"I think I just remember when I was that age, every loss was so low, and every win was so high. I think there's lessons to be learned in the losses.

"She seems a little bit more mature than maybe I was at 18, but I feel like sometimes the losses for me felt so low.

"So I think it's just important getting her to know that she's playing good-level tennis, and I think today it just went my way.

"I am someone who played well young too, so it doesn't always matter. Sometimes it does matter, and you just learn those lessons and I know that she will be in many more fourth rounds and quarters, and she'll capitalise on those moments the next time."

Andreeva up next as quarter-final line-up complete

The impressive victory set up a last-eight meeting with French Open champion Mirra Andreeva, whom Gauff has beaten in all five of their career meetings.

With Gauff's win, the woman's quarter final line-up is set as Aryna Sabalenka plays Linda Noskova and Jessica Pegula takes on Emma Navarro.

Gauff then faces Andreeva, with Qinwen Zheng against Elena Rybakina for a place in the final four at Flushing Meadows.

"It is another tough match," Gauff added. "Mirra is someone that I always have tough matches with and they have leaned my way but every match could have almost gone either way.

"She is obviously in a different mindset now at the top of the game coming off of a Grand Slam win. I expect her to approach the match completely differently than she did in the past."

articles.title: US Open 2026: Alexander Zverev reaches quarter-finals in rare pre-midnight finish in New York
articles.summary: World No 87 Arthur Gea missed out on becoming the first lucky loser to reach a Grand Slam quarter-final as he lost to Botic van de Zandschulp, who awaits as Alexander Zverev's last eight opponent; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis
articles.body:
The top-seeded German cruised through the opening two sets before fending off a Darderi fightback in the third to win 6-2 6-2 7-6(3).

It would mark the first time Zverev has finished a match before midnight in New York this tournament having played four successive night-session matches, including two five-setters.

The 2020 finalist, who has previously finished games at times of 1:55am, 2:15am and 1:09am, was able to see the funny side of a rare early night at 11.48pm.

"I don't know what to do with ​myself, because it's before midnight," said Zverev. "I might go to a practice court, or a bar... that was a joke, so ‌relax. I'm feeling happy, compared to the first two matches the level has been going up."

Zverev is the only man to reach the quarter-finals of all four Grand Slams this year and will now face Botic van de Zandschulp in the final four following the Dutchman's win over lucky loser Arthur Gea.

"I ⁠thought that my level was consistent, but he started incredibly well in third set," Zverev added of his performance.

"I barely saw anyone hit so hard so consistently. He ⁠made it very difficult for me. I'm ​happy to be in the quarter-finals and playing this way."

Next opponent Van de Zandschulp had denied France's world No 87 Gea the chance to become the first lucky loser to reach a Grand Slam quarter-final in a 3-6 6-7 (0-7) 7-6 (9-7) 7-6 (7-3) 6-4 win lasting five hours and 13 minutes.

"I think he's an impressive player," said Zverev of Van de Zandschulp. "I think this might be his favourite tournament in the world, because I think he made a few quarter-finals here before. Obviously he knows how to play well on these courts, and I look forward to having a tough battle."

Belgium's Alexander Blockx meanwhile fought through injury to beat Argentina's Francisco Cerundolo and reach his first Grand Slam quarter-final.

The 28th seed clinched a 6-3 4-6 7-5 7-5 victory before admitting he considered retiring hurt due to a rib issue.

"It was really tough from the beginning of the match. I was struggling a lot, especially while serving. It kept getting worse throughout the match," said the 21-year-old.

"I was really close to retiring, to be honest. I was just hanging in there, but if I would have lost the third set, I think the chances were really high of me retiring.

He will now play Karen Khachanov after the Russian's 7-5, 4-6, 6-7 (6), 6-1, 6-4 win over the USA's Learner Tien.

articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz se enteró a última hora de la noche del domingo que su rival en los cuartos del US Open será el local Ben Shelton. El número nueve mundial y octavo cabeza de serie del cuadro se deshizo de Stefanos Tsitsipas en la ronda de octavos. Shelton ha cedido los tres precedentes con el murciano, el último de ellos en los octavos de Roland Garros 2025. El estadounidense viene en forma como lo demuestra su título en el Masters 1000 de Montreal en el inicio de la gira americana de pista dura. Su mejor resultado en el cuarto grande del calendario fueron las semifinales de 2023. El partido de cuartos del US Open entre Carlos Alcaraz y Ben Shelton se disputará este martes 8 de septiembre en la central Arthur Ashe, del Billie Jean King Tennis Center, en el último turno de la sesión nocturna. El partido empezará sobre las 2:30 horas de la madrugada del martes al miércoles en horario peninsular. Tras superar las rondas previas con solvencia, Carlos Alcaraz afronta un duro examen ante el potente servicio de Ben Shelton en el Arthur Ashe, con la mirada puesta en unas semifinales donde se cruzaría con el vencedor del duelo estadounidense entre Frances Tiafoe y Alex Michelsen. Tras superar con solvencia a Tommy Paul en octavos, Carlos Alcaraz (2.º cabeza de serie) afronta este martes los cuartos de final ante el estadounidense Ben Shelton (8). articles.title: US Open 2026: Carlos Alcaraz can end American dreams by beating Ben Shelton, plus Frances Tiafoe or Alex Michelsen, in New York
articles.summary: Three Americans have the chance to become the first home US Open men's champion since 2003. But Carlos Alcaraz stands in the way.
articles.body:
It could be Carlos Alcaraz versus the United States over the next few days.

The Spanish superstar's popularity at the US Open might be severely tested if he single-handedly prevents an American having the chance to become the first home men's singles champion in 23 years.

Three American players - Ben Shelton, Frances Tiafoe and Alex Michelsen - remain in the draw. All three are in the same half as Alcaraz.

On Tuesday, the defending champion takes on eighth seed Shelton in the quarter-finals.

If the seven-time major winner comes through that blockbuster clash, he will face either Tiafoe or Michelsen in the semi-finals.

And if Alcaraz wins again to reach the Flushing Meadows final, the host nation's long wait for somebody to finally follow in Andy Roddick's 2003 footsteps continues.

Alcaraz says he expects to be facing 24,000 New Yorkers on Arthur Ashe Stadium as well as Shelton, who is looking to reach his second US Open semi-final.

"I think he [will] use the crowd, the people behind him, especially when he's playing here at home," said Alcaraz.

If Ashe can help 23-year-old Shelton earn his first career win over Alcaraz, there is guaranteed to be an American player in the final.

Home stars reaching the men's semi-finals has not been uncommon this century, but only Taylor Fritz has reached the final - two years ago when he lost to Jannik Sinner - since Roddick was beaten by Roger Federer in the 2006 final.

Tiafoe, who is seeded 11th, lost to Fritz in another all-American semi-final and was also eliminated by Alcaraz at the same stage in 2022.

Now the 28-year-old is aiming for a third opportunity to reach his first Grand Slam final.

Tiafoe reached the Cincinnati final last month and, thriving off the energy of the New York crowd, has maintained his momentum.

On what it is like to receive such support, he said: "It's an out-of-body experience, no question. No real explaining that type of feeling.

"It's like you're not even touching the ground at one point. Energy is so high, and it seems like the level of play matches that."

While Tiafoe is one of the sport's great entertainers, 22-year-old Michelsen is more understated.

The world number 46 admits he has been happy to fly "under the radar" at Flushing Meadows while the likes of Tiafoe, Shelton, Fritz and Tommy Paul soak up the attention.

But earning a place in a Grand Slam quarter-final for the first time, and not dropping a set on his way, means Michelsen will find himself under the spotlight on Ashe.

"First, second, third rounds, all matches I'm feeling nerves. It's a human experience," he said.

"But it's just about going out there and managing them to the best of my ability. I feel like I've done that very well."

Six men and women from the United States have reached the last eight at Flushing Meadows this year - the highest tally since 2002 - with three players in each draw.

Along with Tiafoe or Michelsen in the men's, the home fans know they are guaranteed to see at least one American reach the women's semi-finals.

Third seed Jessica Pegula, who is yet to land a major title despite her consistency on the WTA Tour, meets Emma Navarro in another all-American clash on Tuesday.

Coco Gauff - who sits on the other side of the draw - can join Pegula or Navarro by beating Russian fifth seed Mirra Andreeva on Wednesday.

But, unlike the men, there is not a long American drought on the women's side.

Gauff, 22, is looking to win the women's title for the second time, having lifted the trophy in 2023 as a teenager to fulfil the promise she had already long shown.

Pegula, 31, was a beaten finalist in 2024 when she lost to Aryna Sabalenka, who also beat Navarro in the semi-finals that year.

Navarro, 25, has not reached the same stage of a major since, but is rediscovering her best form after stepping back from the tour earlier this season because of health issues.

After beating Russian 21st seed Anna Kalinskaya on Ashe in the last 16, Navarro joked she should have tried getting the home fans on her side before facing Pegula.

"I should have talked to the crowd a little, asking them to come back and cheer me on for that match. I'm definitely going to need them," she said.

articles.title: Wimbledon no acreditará a 'influencers' tras los incidentes en el US Open
articles.standfirst: La 'mala praxis' de los creadores de contenido ha provocado críticas por parte de los tenistas y problemas durante algunos partidos
articles.summary: La 'mala praxis' de los creadores de contenido ha provocado críticas por parte de los tenistas y problemas durante algunos partidos
articles.body: El torneo de Wimbledon no acreditará a 'influencers' y se desmarcará de esta manera de las polémicas surgidas en el actual Abierto de Estados Unidos, donde cerca de un centenar de 'creadores de contenido' fueron acreditados por la organización y provocaron problemas durante la disputa de los partidos. El torneo neoyorquino dio el doble de acreditaciones a 'influencers' de cara a esta edición con el objetivo de atraer a una audiencia mayor, pero las prácticas de los mismos han provocado críticas por parte de los tenistas y problemas durante los partidos. Según medios británicos, la organización de Wimbledon no tiene entre sus planes acreditar a 'influencers' o creadores de contenido, como ha sido la norma habitual hasta ahora. Además, las normas del propio All England Club, el recinto donde se disputa el torneo, impiden que se acceda a los partidos con objetos como aros de luz. El personal acreditado de Wimbledon tiene, además, prohibido grabar vídeo en la mayoría de zonas del club. Durante la disputa del US Open, en uno de los partidos de la cuatro veces ganadora de Grand Slam Naomi Osaka, un grupo de 'influencers' utilizó uno de estos aros de luz, distrayendo a las jugadoras, además de que el juez de silla tuvo que llamar la atención al público en varias ocasiones. La japonesa criticó esta actitud, mientras que Coco Gauff animó a que se sigan las reglas de etiqueta del deporte. También ha habido otro tipo de interrupciones durante algunos encuentros de esta edición del US Open. Aryna Sabalenka, número uno del mundo, paró un partido porque supuestamente alguien estaba fumando marihuana en la grada.

Her background in design has also supported her work in fashion and branding.The couple’s wealth could continue to grow. Paul remains an important part of the new generation of American tennis players, while Lorenze continues to expand her digital and business presence. articles.title: US Open today: Day 10 quarterfinal schedule, scores; Day 11 matchups
articles.summary: The 2026 US Open heads to the quarterfinals, featuring many top seeds competing for places in the men’s and women’s singles semifinals.
articles.body:
The 2026 US Open heads into the quarterfinal stage on Tuesday, Sept. 8, showcasing many of the tournament's top seeds battling for a spot in both the men's and women's singles semifinals.

The day kicks off with the first women's singles quarterfinal, featuring Wworld No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka , who is aiming for her fourth US Open title. She will take on Wimbledon champion and No. 6 seed Linda Noskova , who endured a tense battle against Marta Kostyuk – requiring six match points – to ultimately secure her spot in the quarterfinals.

The second women's quarterfinal sets the stage for an all-American showdown between No. 3 seed Jessica Pegula and No. 26 seed Emma Navarro .

Turning to the men's draw, fans will see another all-American battle as No. 11 seed Frances Tiafoe faces off against the unseeded Alex Michelsen .

The evening session will culminate with a marquee matchup as defending champion Carlos Alcaraz, the No. 2 seed, takes on No. 8 seed Ben Shelton.

Unforgettable US Open 2026 tennis photos from New York
